context_sources.name: Academic Ranking of World Universities, ARWU 2017
World Bank Open Data, education indicators
Project Atlas 2017, Institute of International Education
Salim, Opportunities for Higher Education, entry barriers

limitations: A watermark and running header leak glyphs into every page and into the equations.
The gender equity formula is garbled; only the prose definition survives.
The normalization denominator is scrambled but matches the standard vector form cited.
All numerical results except the printed totals sit in figures and cannot be rechecked from text.

tasks: Build a cross-country model of health and sustainability
Score several countries and choose one with room to improve
Set a vision and score it against the present with a time model
Propose policies and a schedule and test their effect
Discuss the real impact and admit the difficulty

section_map.summary: Three dimensions, five indices, India chosen for the lowest score, four five-year plans to 2037.
No standard exists yet, and change takes a long time. Five tasks, the last one to admit difficulty.
Stable university count, one definition of spending, reliable web data, no disasters.
Five index formulas, then the same normalization scored across countries and down time.
Five countries scored; India lowest and least balanced.
Three weak indices, a tiered vision, policies, and the interests each policy offends.
Shifts of 5 and 10 percent move the score linearly.
Four strengths, three weaknesses, one of them the model's silence under disaster.

contributions.summary: A score declared meaningless except by comparison, then built entirely out of comparison.
An enrollment target tiered by population group instead of applied flat.
Each policy followed by the interest it offends.

dependency_graph.handoff: The five indices are the columns of the cross-country scoring matrix
The same five indices, dated, are the columns of the time scoring matrix
The vision targets fill the future rows that the vertical model scores
The lowest and least balanced country, and the best rate in the set, drive the vision

assumptions.summary: University numbers move too slowly to matter inside one plan.
No war, crisis, disaster or attack during the twenty years.
The top 30 percent can reach the best enrollment rate in the comparison set.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: 2017 data from ARWU, Webometrics, Project Atlas and the World Bank, named per factor.

models.summary: Five indices from products and ratios of reported statistics.
Column normalization scaled to 20 and summed, across countries.
The same scoring down a time axis, present against planned.
Tiered enrollment target plus three schedules.

verification.summary: Each indicator shifted 5 and 10 percent; the score moves linearly, as the formula implies.

results_trace.summary: 2017 scores: Australia 53.8, India 23.29, Japan 23.54, Sweden 48.13, Britain 49.01.
India leads expenditure, trails research, enrollment and internationalization.
Vertical model: India from 24.79 in 2017 to 57.96 in 2037.

writing_logic.summary: The introduction states that change is slow before any model is built.
India is chosen over Japan for being less balanced, not only for scoring lower.
The benefit is stated and then undercut by the admission that the policies offend the powerful.

language_observations.summary: The lowest score is glossed in the same clause as the largest room for improvement.
Standardization is justified by the nuisance it removes, differing units.
A high spending ratio is conceded in parentheses and then overruled.
A score is called meaningless unless it comes from comparison.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Saying a lone score means nothing forces every later number to earn its place by comparison.
A target that discounts for the excluded group reads as more serious than a flat national target.
Naming the people a policy harms, including the group whose support it needs, reads as judgment.

weaknesses.summary: The method is labelled TOPSIS but never builds an ideal solution or a distance.
The 2017 score is 23.29 across countries and 24.79 across time, with no reconciliation.
Authors: accuracy depends on web data, some parameters are subjective, and disasters are ignored.

independent_extensions.summary: Either drop the TOPSIS name or add the ideal point and the separation measure.
Derive the catch-up fractions instead of setting them at 0.1 to 0.4.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Normalize before summing indices that carry different units, and say why.
State the policy, then the mechanism, then who is hurt.

unresolved_questions.question: What is the exact form of the gender equity index?
Why does India score 23.29 in one model and 24.79 in the other for the same year?
